subject: Rerank & classifier pricing: per-score billing and package options
messages:
From: Sarah Patel <sarah@acmeai.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acmeai.com
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Rerank & classifier billing question

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the product overview yesterday — really helpful. Procurement asked me to get a clear, line-item explanation of how Redwood bills for the caller-facing reranker and for the classifier endpoint we intend to use for document labeling. Two specific questions:

1) If we send a single search request with 50 candidates and ask the reranker to score all 50, is that counted as 1 API call or 50 billable scoring operations?
2) For classifiers (batch labeling of documents), do you bill per document, per API call, or by token? We expect to label ~120k docs/month.

Can you send a short rate-card snippet and any packaged discount thresholds you typically offer for customers at our scale?

Appreciate it — can loop in legal/procurement once we have a clear sheet.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Patel
Director, Search Product
Acme AI
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Patel <sarah@acmeai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Rerank & classifier billing question

Sarah — thanks for the clear questions. I pulled together a short breakdown and attached our Q2 rate card and a draft SOW for the integration. High level answers below; detail and examples follow.

TL;DR:
- Reranker: billed per candidate scored (so a request scoring 50 candidates = 50 scoring units).
- Classifier: billed per input document labeled; token billing only applies to free-form text generation endpoints, not to deterministic classification decisions.
- We offer step discounts at volume bands and a predictable committed-usage package for enterprise customers (example math below).

Quick examples (to illustrate):
- Rerank call with 50 candidates: billed as 50 scoring units. If you use batch scoring (grouping candidates across calls) you still pay per candidate scored.
- Classifier: 120k docs/month = 120k classifier units. If you attach metadata or request explainability tokens, there may be small token charges on top but core classifier unit is per document.

See the attached PDF for current list rates and our standard Managed Tier discounts (10% at $50k/month, 18% at $200k/month committed). Happy to sketch an Acme-specific committed package.

Full breakdown and worked examples below.

— Tessa

Adding a couple of packaging notes from pricing:

- Metering nuance: for rerankers we meter candidate scoring units and also expose an optional "per-call" surcharge for extremely low-latency dedicated pools (this shows up only if you opt into Dedicated GPU pools with SLA-backed latency).
- Bundles: we can structure either a usage-only plan (pay-as-you-go at list rates), a committed usage package with stepped discounts, or a hybrid with reserved QPS (reduces per-score price by ~12% at equivalent commit).
- Credits & trials: for the POC we can offer a one-time 25k candidate credit to validate integration. Credits are applied before usage billing.

If you can share an expected QPS and an average candidate count per query, I can run a 12-month cost forecast and show the break-even point for committing.

Best,
Marissa

Redwood Inference

Thanks — helpful. A couple of clarifications from our engineers and procurement:

- Example workload: ~3k user queries/day, average 30 candidates/query during peak, ~120k classifier labels/month (pipeline runs nightly).
- Can you show sample math: monthly cost for (a) pure PAYG, (b) 12-month commit with 15% discount, (c) reserved QPS hybrid? Procurement wants approximate dollar figures to discuss internally.
- On the reranker, do you charge for candidates that are filtered server-side before scoring (e.g., we call a filter endpoint that removes ~10 candidates before submitting 40 to rerank)? We want to avoid being billed for pre-filtered items.

Also, procurement asked whether you can provide SOC2 evidence and a 3-year retention option in the SOW (we flagged compliance earlier).

Regards,

Sarah — great context; below is the worked math and answers to the procurement points. I'll also loop in our Security & Compliance pack after this thread for SOC 2 artifacts.

Worked monthly cost (approx):
- Inputs: 3k queries/day * 30 candidates/query * 30 days = 2,700,000 candidates/month scored. Classifier: 120,000 docs/month.

A) PAYG (list rates)
- Rerank scoring unit price (list): $0.00018 per candidate scored -> 2,700,000 * $0.00018 = $486.00/month
- Classifier unit price (list): $0.00035 per document -> 120,000 * $0.00035 = $42.00/month
- Estimated total PAYG = $528.00/month

B) 12-month commit with 15% discount (applied to usage)
- Rerank after discount: $0.000153 per candidate -> 2,700,000 * $0.000153 = $413.10
- Classifier after discount: $0.0002975 per doc -> 120,000 * $0.0002975 = $35.70
- Estimated total commit = $448.80/month (commit required: ~$5,386/year)

C) Reserved QPS hybrid (reserved 150 QPS peak, reduces per-score by ~12%)
- Effective rerank price: $0.0001584 per candidate -> 2,700,000 * $0.0001584 = $427.68
- Classifier price unchanged in this example: $42.00
- Estimated hybrid total = $469.68/month

Notes & policy clarifications:
- Filtered candidates: we only bill for scoring operations actually executed by the reranker. If you perform upstream filtering and send 40 candidates to the reranker, we bill 40 scoring units. Server-side filtering that never invokes the scoring kernel won't be billed. If you use a Redwood "pre-filter" API that performs indexing/filtering carried out on Redwood's infrastructure, that may have separate metering; we'll call that out explicitly in the SOW if you adopt it.
- Attachments & compliance: included the SOC 2 checklist and retention options in the Drive link; we can add a 3-year data retention clause to the SOW and flag any additional cost if retention exceeds our default enterprise retention tier.
- Credits: we can provision the 25k candidate POC credit Marissa mentioned as a one-time line item in the quote.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Marissa to provide a formal quote PDF reflecting PAYG vs commit vs hybrid (I asked her offline to prepare).
2) Acme to confirm whether you want the 25k POC credit and whether the SOW should include 3-year retention.
3) I'll have Security share SOC 2 artifacts and an addendum for retention once you confirm SOW preferences.

Happy to hop on a 30-min call to walk procurement through the numbers.

— Tessa
